violations.why: Force ISR (prio 3) can preempt Timer_A between the read and write of timerCount++, so its update is lost.
Force ISR preempts the increment and sets timerCount to 0, then Timer_A writes back a stale value.
Force ISR can run between the increment and the check, so the check sees 0 instead of the incremented value.
Force ISR can overwrite timerCount between the increment and the check in Timer_A.
Force ISR preempts Timer_B between setting timerCount=1 and checking it, so the check sees 0 and the branch is skipped.
Force ISR can preempt Timer_B between the write and the read of timerCount, changing the value that is read.
